paragraphs: Here's what this passage is really about, friend. These settlers did worship the LORD, and they also served their own gods (2 Kings 17:33). They wanted the LORD on the shelf right next to the idols, like one more flavor in the box. But the LORD never asked to be one of the options.

Look at what He told Israel back in the covenant: "Do not worship other gods." He said it in 2 Kings 17:35, again in verse 37, and again in verse 38. When God says the same thing three times, I'm not going to treat it like a suggestion. He wants all of you, not a slice. And the sad part is that verse 41 says their children and grandchildren kept doing as their fathers did.

So ask yourself, baker: what's sitting on my shelf next to Him? Maybe it's not a carved idol. Maybe it's the thing I run to first, the thing I trust to rescue me. The LORD promised, "He will deliver you from the hands of all your enemies" (2 Kings 17:39), and the way to that promise is worshiping Him alone. Keep your heart's oven for Him and nobody else.
